newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, Russia supports.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, Russia supports.

text.p: London's spot August white sugar contract held steady on Tuesday afternoon but although the market was supported by talk of Russian buying, volume was thin in the absence of major players.
Commission houses were said to be the dominant force behind the day's thin volume, although some trade interest was also seen.
Spreads were relatively inactive with most of the August activity reported to be flat price, though volume was boosted by light Paris/London arbitrage deals.
"The Russian offtake is the reason why the market is higher, supposedly...but people are a little dubious about selling and also about going short of August," said one trader.
"I think being long of August/October is what most trade people would like to be."
At 1645 GMT August stood 40 cents higher at $318.80 and October was down 10 cents at $308.10. Volume totalled a scant 395 lots, most of which was in August.
Since bursting higher by around $3 at the start of last week, August has been content to trade between $316 and $319 -- but daily ranges have been tight and activity generally light.
Analysts pegged immediate resistance at a series of $318.80 highs but said $323.00 could be another upside objective in the short term.

But although August's 10-day momentum indicator has ticked slightly up from its downwards slope, suggesting that more gains could be on the cards, the shorter-term five-day line is poised to head into negative territory.
Just 210 lots were traded in Paris, nearly all of which was in August. The position was up 50 cents at $318.50, while October was untraded.
